title: Catalogue search, sorting and category filter

sourcesRead.contributes: user story, rule that web shop and API behave the same, catalogue API endpoints and response shape, AC 1-7, category-id note, out of scope

actors: mobile app (consumer of the public catalogue API)
context: As a shopper I want to search, sort and filter the tool catalogue so that I find the right tool quickly.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Searching the web shop for a term shows only products whose name contains the term, and a caption "Searched for: <term>".
acceptanceCriteria.text: Searching the web shop for a term shows only products whose name contains the term, and a caption "Searched for: <term>".
outcomes: every product shown has a name that contains the searched term, regardless of letter case (G6, provided by the user)
caption "Searched for: <term>" is shown

acceptanceCriteria.quote: GET /products/search?q=<term> returns 200 with only products whose name contains the term, regardless of letter case (searching "PLIERS" finds the same products as "pliers").
acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /products/search?q=<term> returns 200 with only products whose name contains the term, regardless of letter case (searching "PLIERS" finds the same products as "pliers").
outcomes: GET /products/search?q=<term> returns 200
every product in data has a name that contains the term, regardless of letter case
searching "PLIERS" finds the same products as "pliers"

acceptanceCriteria.quote: A search without matches shows "There are no products found." on the web shop, and the API returns 200 with an empty data list and total 0.
acceptanceCriteria.text: A search without matches shows "There are no products found." on the web shop, and the API returns 200 with an empty data list and total 0.
outcomes: web shop: a search without matches shows "There are no products found."
API: GET /products/search with a term without matches returns 200
API: data is an empty list
API: total is 0

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Choosing "Price (Low - High)" on the web shop lists the products by ascending price; GET /products?sort=price,asc returns the products in ascending price order.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Choosing "Price (Low - High)" on the web shop lists the products by ascending price; GET /products?sort=price,asc returns the products in ascending price order.
outcomes: web shop: after choosing "Price (Low - High)" the products are listed by ascending price
API: GET /products?sort=price,asc returns 200 (G3, provided by the user)
API: GET /products?sort=price,asc returns the products in ascending price order

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Filtering the web shop by the category "Hammer" shows only hammers; GET /products?by_category=<id of Hammer> returns only products in that category.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Filtering the web shop by the category "Hammer" shows only hammers; GET /products?by_category=<id of Hammer> returns only products in that category.
outcomes: web shop: filtering by the category "Hammer" shows only hammers (products in the Hammer category)
API: GET /products?by_category=<id of Hammer> returns 200 (G3, provided by the user)
API: GET /products?by_category=<id of Hammer> returns only products in the Hammer category

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Results are paginated with 12 products per page (per_page 12) on the web shop and in the API.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Results are paginated with 12 products per page (per_page 12) on the web shop and in the API.
outcomes: web shop: a full page of results shows 12 products
API: GET /products returns 200 (G3, provided by the user)
API: the response has per_page 12
API: a full page holds 12 products in data

acceptanceCriteria.quote: An empty search (no term) returns all products, so the mobile app can reuse the search endpoint for its "All tools" screen.
acceptanceCriteria.text: An empty search (no term) returns all products, so the mobile app can reuse the search endpoint for its "All tools" screen.
outcomes: GET /products/search?q= (q with no value, G5) returns 200 (G3)
the answer is a normal paginated answer whose total equals the whole catalogue, the same total as GET /products (G4, provided by the user)

endpoints.request: query parameters sort (e.g. ?sort=price,asc) and by_category (e.g. ?by_category=<id of Hammer>); auth none from "the public catalogue API" (story.md#L18)
?q=<term>; auth none from "the public catalogue API" (story.md#L18)
source of category ids (e.g. the id of Hammer for by_category)

rules.text: The web shop and the public catalogue API (used by our mobile app) must behave the same way.

testData.strategy: not stated in the sources; the criteria only read the existing catalogue
constraints: the catalogue has products found by searching "pliers" (story.md#L24)

gaps.element: where the id of the category "Hammer" is in the GET /categories/tree answer (nesting, field names), and how a product's category is seen in the product data and on the web shop to check "only hammers"

tried.result: story.md#L32 names the endpoint only; story.md#L20 does not list product fields

GET /categories/tree answers a JSON array of top-level nodes {id, name, slug, parent_id, sub_categories:[nodes]}; 'Hammer' is a sub-category of 'Hand Tools' (id 01M44NSB700A1N91T5WRW6YVJH, a string ULID). A product's category is the nested object category {id, name, slug} in the product data; on the web shop the card shows no category, so 'only hammers' is checked against the API's products whose category.id is the Hammer id
